explain.say: About 50 million years ago, India crashed into Asia. Neither plate would sink, so the rock between them crumpled and folded upward, like a rug pushed against a wall. The old seabed was lifted high, fossils and all. Can you see now why there are fossils on Everest?

faq.a: The Indian plate crashed into the Eurasian plate about 50 million years ago. Neither would sink easily, so the crust between them crumpled, folded and piled up into the highest mountains on Earth.
asks: What kind of mountains are the Himalayas?

faq.q: Why are there sea fossils on Mount Everest?
faq.a: The rock near the top formed as limestone on the floor of an ancient ocean between India and Asia. When the plates collided, that seabed was squeezed and lifted up into the mountains.
asks: How did seashells get to the top of Everest?

faq.a: Yes. India still moves north about 4 to 5 cm a year, pushing the mountains up by a few millimetres a year, while rain, rivers and ice wear them down.
Pangaea was a supercontinent that joined almost all the land on Earth, about 300 to 200 million years ago. It slowly broke apart into the continents we know today.
Mount Everest is 8,848.86 metres tall, a height announced jointly by China and Nepal in 2020. In Nepal it is called Sagarmatha, and in Tibetan Chomolungma.
asks: What is the highest mountain in the world?

facts: The official height of Mount Everest, announced by China and Nepal in 2020, is 8,848.86 m.
The rock at the summit of Everest is marine limestone containing fossils of sea creatures.
The Indian plate still moves north at about 4 to 5 cm per year.

quiz.say: What happened about 50 million years ago to start building the Himalayas?
quiz.why: The Indian plate collided with Asia, and the rock between them folded upward into mountains.

wrong.1: The Himalayas are fold mountains, not volcanoes.
wrong.2: No meteorite made the Himalayas; moving plates did.
